title: Availability commitment and definition
status_rationale: No production service, uptime history, SLA, status page or service-credit terms exist as of 2026-11-25.
target_answer: Echelon publishes capability-level service levels rather than a single uptime figure: separate monthly targets for read access to records and statements, for submission of requests, and for approval and payment dispatch, measured with a stated methodology. A deliberate fail-closed refusal of a financial action because safety cannot be confirmed is reported transparently as unavailability of that capability, not excluded. Exclusions are limited and enumerated; scheduled maintenance counts against the target unless within a pre-announced window under a defined monthly cap.
current_practice: Not established. CNV-EXP-001 requires service levels to be measured with a stated methodology before publication.
intended_practice: Publish SLOs only after measurement exists in a production-like environment.
customer_statement: Echelon does not currently offer an availability SLA because no production service exists. We intend to publish capability-level service levels once we can measure them.

challenge.customer_intent: Know how reliably the service will be there when needed.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Service unavailable at critical moments without recourse.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: A single 99.9 percent uptime number, usually measured by the vendor with broad exclusions, says little about whether money movement worked and can hide partial outages.
challenge.contractually_required: Yes, almost universally expected in enterprise SaaS contracts.
challenge.historical_convention: Hosting-era uptime SLAs measured at the network edge.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Not applicable; availability is a measured outcome.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Measurement and credit calculation can be automated.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Raw probe data per capability and tenant.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Capability-level SLOs with customer-recomputable raw data, counting fail-closed refusals honestly.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, if raw data is shared.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Uncertain: procurement templates expect one percentage; a lower figure for payment dispatch may look worse than competitors.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If capability-level SLOs are too complex for customers to use in their own risk assessments.
challenge.alternative_risks: Honest fail-closed accounting lowers reported availability relative to competitors who exclude it.
supporting_arguments: Aligns the metric with the customer's real concern.
Removes incentive to fail open to protect an uptime number.
opposing_arguments: Customers may still require a single headline figure.

title: Availability measurement and reporting
status_rationale: No production service, uptime history, SLA, status page or service-credit terms exist as of 2026-11-25.
target_answer: Availability is measured by synthetic probes from at least two external vantage points per capability and by server-side success ratios per tenant, so partial outages affecting some tenants or features are counted. Monthly per-tenant reports are generated automatically, and customers can obtain the raw measurement data to recompute them or compare with their own monitoring. Historical availability is published once a production record exists.
current_practice: Not established. MON-018 specifies monitoring of operational resilience signals.
intended_practice: Implement measurement before any SLA is offered.
provable: Nothing. There is no uptime history because there is no production service.
customer_statement: We have no uptime history because no production service exists. We plan per-tenant, externally measured availability reporting with raw data available to customers.
owner: Proposed: SRE Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Status page, outage notification and post-incident reports
status_rationale: No production service, uptime history, SLA, status page or service-credit terms exist as of 2026-11-25.
target_answer: A component-level status page hosted independently of production shows current status and history; customers can subscribe by email and webhook. Customers are notified of a material outage within 30 minutes of detection, which is designed to satisfy the bank service provider obligation to notify affected banking organizations as soon as possible when covered services are materially disrupted for four or more hours. A root-cause report follows within ten business days of a qualifying incident.
intended_practice: Stand up an independent status page before the first customer.
customer_statement: No status page exists yet. We plan an independently hosted status page and defined notification times before production.
owner: Proposed: SRE Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Maintenance windows and change-related downtime
status_rationale: No production service, uptime history, SLA, status page or service-credit terms exist as of 2026-11-25.
target_answer: Deployments are zero-downtime by default and schema changes are applied online through Strata-managed migrations with expand-and-contract patterns. Any planned downtime is announced at least five business days ahead, scheduled outside customer business hours, capped monthly, and prohibited during declared freeze periods such as the last two weeks of December. Emergency maintenance is announced as soon as it is decided, with reason.
current_practice: Not established. Strata can compute schema diffs in pilot status; no deployment pipeline for Unbound exists.
intended_practice: Design the release pipeline for zero downtime from the start.
customer_statement: We have not set maintenance windows because no production service exists. We intend zero-downtime deployments and change freezes at year-end.
owner: Proposed: SRE Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Service credits and remedies
status_rationale: No production service, uptime history, SLA, status page or service-credit terms exist as of 2026-11-25.
target_answer: Service credits are calculated automatically from the measurement stream and applied without a claim process; repeated misses (for example three months in any six) give the customer a termination right without penalty and transition assistance. Credits are not the exclusive remedy for failures caused by breach of security or data-integrity obligations.
current_practice: Not established; no contract templates located.
intended_practice: Draft SLA schedule with counsel when SLOs are measurable.
customer_statement: We do not currently offer service credits. Remedies will be defined when a service level agreement is offered.
owner: Proposed: Finance Lead (role not yet staffed)
open_questions: Will Echelon's commercial counsel accept credits that are not the exclusive remedy?

title: Subprocessor dependency and its effect on availability
status_rationale: No production service, uptime history, SLA, status page or service-credit terms exist as of 2026-11-25.
target_answer: Each capability is mapped to the subprocessors it depends on (cloud hosting, managed PostgreSQL, identity, email delivery, payment connectivity, custodian feeds, charity registries, AI providers). Echelon's SLA does not exclude outages of its own chosen subprocessors; it does distinguish outages of parties the customer chose, such as the sponsor's bank or custodian. Provider status is shown on the status page and in the product.
current_practice: Not established. RR-REQ-X-073-r2 specifies a critical-vendor register; UNB-API-STD-005 requires documented provider outage behavior per integration.
intended_practice: Build the register at provider selection.
customer_statement: No production subprocessors have been selected. We plan to publish which providers each function depends on.
owner: Proposed: Vendor Risk Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Degraded modes and fail-closed financial actions
status_rationale: No production service, uptime history, SLA, status page or service-credit terms exist as of 2026-11-25.
target_answer: Every dependency outage maps to an explicit degraded state. Read access, drafting and non-financial work continue; money movement, payee changes and authority changes fail closed when the system cannot confirm safety (for example the hold registry is stale beyond its freshness bound or database quorum is lost), and the user sees a distinct, honest status such as 'Outcome being confirmed' rather than a false success or a generic error. Platform-originated holds are time-bounded, notify the sponsor's designated officer, never move funds, and leave the sponsor able to pay through its own bank.
current_practice: Not established. CNV-PLT-007, UNB-CUST-022, UNB-INV-037, UNB-EXT-036 and UNB-UX-003 specify the behavior.
intended_practice: Implement degraded states as typed domain states with automated tests per dependency.
provable: Nothing beyond requirement text and Forma presentation components, which exist in a separate design-system repository.
customer_statement: Our design stops money movement when safety cannot be confirmed while keeping other functions available, and tells users plainly what state a payment is in. This has not been built or tested.

challenge.customer_intent: Keep working during partial outages without risking incorrect payments.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Either total outage from a minor dependency failure, or unsafe payments made on stale data.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Conventional availability engineering treats any refusal as failure, which pressures systems to fail open; questionnaires rarely ask what the system does when it cannot confirm safety.
challenge.legally_required: No. Sanctions and payment rules make the originator (the sponsor) liable for unsafe payments, which is why fail-closed protects the customer.
challenge.historical_convention: Batch systems queued everything and reconciled later.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Unsafe dispatch on stale hold data is eliminated in scope by an atomic fencing check at dispatch.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Typed degraded states; dispatch requires a fresh safety proof.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Fail closed for money, fail open for reading, and report both honestly.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, by test results and by status history.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely among compliance officers; uncertain among users who want payments to go out.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If fail-closed periods are long and frequent enough that sponsors route around the platform.
challenge.alternative_risks: Over-conservative freshness bounds could block payments unnecessarily at peak.
supporting_arguments: Protects the sponsor from liability for unsafe payments.
Users are never told a payment succeeded when it did not.
opposing_arguments: Users may perceive the system as unreliable.
